scope: Every Realtek NIC that is up on a production PC with a Dante leg (docs/two-networks.md, scope). One entry per chip and OS; a Realtek adapter without an entry fails until it is measured and added. Read-only checkers: tools/windows/nic-standard-check.ps1, tools/linux/nic-standard-check.py.

fields.match: windows: hardware_id prefixes of the device's first hardware id (case-insensitive); linux: usb or pci vendor:product ids (lowercase hex)
fields.driver: windows: allowed, a list of objects, each a file (an allowed DriverFileName, any case, named once) with its own optional min_version and evidence; linux: modules and an optional firmware; both: bad (a file, a version, or both, that fails, with evidence), status, evidence, plan. Every object takes only its documented keys: an unknown key is refused
fields.expected: a string, or a list of strings any of which passes; null with status report
fields.compare: equals (default), bits (every bit of expected is set), contains (the value holds the expected text)
fields.absent: fail (default): the keyword must be there; pass: a driver without the keyword passes
fields.status: settled: decided with its evidence; open: the standard value until the named measurement decides; report: no standard value yet, printed, never a failure
fields.profile: low_latency: checked only with the low_latency profile (iemmixer gen3, dasio); every other value holds for every profile
fields.evidence: a ticket, a measurement or a vendor document; 'none yet: fleet value' where the working PCs already share the value and nothing measured it
fields.eee: the vendor-independent rule, checked on every wired physical NIC of the PC (any vendor, with or without an entry, up or down): windows keywords (any case) whose value must be in off; any other keyword whose display_name matches the pattern is judged by its display value (display_off passes, display_on fails, else INFO); linux off lists the passing ethtool --show-eee states (enabled - active and enabled - inactive are enabled). Patterns are regular expressions matched without regard to case

eee.name: Energy-Efficient Ethernet off on every wired NIC
eee.scope: every wired physical NIC of a rig PC, whatever the vendor or chip (Realtek, Intel, Aquantia, any), up or down, with or without an entry in adapters
eee.evidence: the owner, 20.11.2026: EEE enabled on any of our rig devices is a serious failure (dstack #465); power saving off on every wired NIC (owner 7.11.2026, songplayer#285). Keywords: Realtek *EEE, EEE, AdvancedEEE, EnableGreenEthernet (read on resolume-snv, resolume-pp, mbc, dsg, FOH 20.11.2026), Intel EEELinkAdvertisement and *EEE; an Aquantia (Marvell AQtion) or any other driver's EEE keyword by its display name (no Windows Aquantia NIC in the fleet to read its keyword). Realtek's EEEMaxSupportSpeed is a speed, not a switch: INFO

adapters.covers: RTL8156 and RTL8156B (USB 2.5GbE): one USB id. Every one in the fleet is an RTL8156B (bcdDevice 0x31xx; Realtek's 1156.22 INF matches REV_31F4 to its RTL8156B section; Linux firmware rtl8156b-2). No RTL8156 (non-B) is in use.

allowed.evidence: Realtek's NetAdapterCx driver 11.19.602.2025 carries the transmit-queue keywords and measured clean against the inbox driver (dstack #425, songplayer#337). Fleet: resolume-snv and resolume-pp.

Realtek's newer NetAdapterCx package 1156.22.113.2026 (oem69.inf, Realtek Gaming USB 2.5GbE Family Controller) on mbc-snv at PendingTransmits 8 / TransmitBufferLen 64 since 21.11.2026 12:46 CET (dasio peer 25.11.2026). dcontroller's per-second max arrival lateness 21.11 12:50-14:36 CET: stream-obs <- mbc p50 1125, p99 1729, p999 3041, max 3083 us against a 13041 us latency, 0 over it; MBC-SNV-dlisten <- mbc p50 854, p99 927, max 1239 us. The same as before at 3/37 (p99 1708, max 3270 us): no change beyond noise (dasio#24, comments of 21.11). The owner's rule is the newest Realtek driver, not an old pin.

bad.evidence: Microsoft's inbox NetAdapterCx driver 11.4.211.2022: a 3-URB / 18-buffer send queue, no PendingTransmits keyword; 6400-9700 late Dante packets a busy minute at dsg against 198 an hour on 11.19.602.2025 at 8 / 64 (dstack #425, songplayer#337)
Realtek's NDIS driver 10.68.20: USB/WDF DPCs up to 19.3 ms against 0.28 ms on the Cx driver, A/B on mbc 18.11.2026 (dstack #290)

driver.evidence: Realtek's NetAdapterCx drivers, each at its own minimum: 11.19.602.2025 carries the transmit-queue keywords and measured clean against the inbox driver (dstack #425, songplayer#337); the newer package 1156.22.113.2026 ran the #290 A/B on mbc (DPCs under 0.3 ms against NDIS) and, at the standard's 8 / 64 queue, read the same Dante lateness as at 3 / 37 on the same driver (dasio#24, dasio peer 25.11.2026; no driver-to-driver lateness comparison); the Cx family against NDIS (dstack #290). The owner's rule is the newest Realtek driver. Fleet: resolume-snv and resolume-pp on 11.19, mbc-snv on 1156.22.

values.name: Transmit URBs
values.evidence: 3 -> 8 (with buffers 18 -> 64): receivers' reorders ~9/h -> ~3/h, the FOH card's peak 9.6 -> 4.7 ms (dstack receiver A/B 10.11.2026, songplayer#255/#285); inbox 3 -> 8 cut dsg's late packets ~100x (dstack #425).
values.plan: 8 vs 32 on resolume-pp with two NDI receivers, by #425's ndiD capture (pktmon on TCPIP / NetAdapterCx / miniport, a detached 60 s capture, .claude/rules/windows-pcs.md): Dante TCPIP -> miniport p99 against 9.4 ms and max against 18.4 ms at 8; the value with the lower p99 and max becomes the standard.

bad.evidence: a 20-30 ms receive DPC every ~100 s on FOH's RTL8125 (dasio#1, 2.11.2026; docs/windows-box.md; dstack's former start-line list), and no later measurement keeps it

driver.evidence: The 20-30 ms receive DPC was measured on 10.72 AND 10.79 on FOH's RTL8125, with 10.39.212.2020 clean there (dasio#1, docs/windows-box.md). dasio then kept 10.79.20.1003 together with its own deferred receive (dasio_pacer RxdEnable: TCP and discovery receive leave the NIC's DPC) and kernel TX; its baseline records 10.79.20.1003 as best and the inbox rtcx21 and 10.39 as worse on that path (dasio's config/baseline-pc-profile.toml, dasio#1, dasio#128). 10.79.20.1003 read clean on dsg's RTL8168 (dstack #383); 10.79.50.1003 on dsg's RTL8168s since 18.11 (the owner's rule on dasio#120, dasio#188: SoundGrid clock losses 78 -> 0). Every rt640x64 PC in the fleet is a dasio host: 10.79 without dasio's deferred receive is NOT measured clean on the RTL8125.
driver.plan: one version for the family: 10.79.50.1003 on FOH's RTL8125 too (dasio's step under dasio#120's rule), then min_version 10.79.50.1003. A PC on rt640x64 without dasio's deferred receive is measured before it carries Dante (10.39.212.2020 is the only version measured clean without it).
